frontend_live.condition: 2 separate layers, check each independently — and for layer (1), TRY TO FIX IT YOURSELF before concluding it's missing, the same self-provisioning spirit as the specialist install map below, just applied to the target app instead of a specialist tool: (1) does the app itself boot locally (a live dev server/preview URL)? If not reachable, look for a `dev`/`start` script in the target repo's own package.json (or equivalent per-stack convention) and start it yourself, detached/backgrounded (don't block on it — a cold Turbopack/webpack start can genuinely take 30s+, confirmed by direct measurement), then poll for reachability with a generous timeout (60s, checking every few seconds) before giving up. Only after that genuine attempt — no dev/start script found, or still unreachable after the timeout — is this 'skipped: no reachable running instance (tried the discovered dev command, still unreachable after Ns)'; a skip that never attempted a start is not this rule's intended outcome. If you started it yourself, track that and stop it again once this flow's report is done (don't leave an orphaned background process) — never stop a server that was already running before you got here, you don't own that one. (2) does the Playwright MCP server itself connect/launch (try one cheap sanity call, e.g. navigate to about:blank, before trusting primary as usable) — missing → 'skipped: Playwright MCP server failed to connect (app itself was reachable)'. frontend_live has no secondary/fallback — a failure at (1) or (2), after the real attempt above, always means skip, never substituted with static reasoning.
frontend_live.note: CONFIRMED 2026-09-25: the naive stdio form (`claude mcp add playwright -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest ...`) genuinely connect-timed-out 3/3 times during a real audit run alongside other work (semgrep scanning, the dev server compiling), even though `claude mcp list` reported it Connected moments before/after. Measured root cause at the time: `npx @playwright/mcp@latest` costs ~5s of network/registry overhead on EVERY spawn (steady-state, not just first-run). v2.1-v2.3 worked around this by switching the default to a standalone HTTP server (a long-lived `playwright-mcp --port 8931 ...` process kept running out-of-band) — re-tested 2/2 clean, but requires a persistent background process, which the user explicitly does not want to run. REVISED 2026-09-27 (this v2.3a), based on further research into Claude Code's own MCP transport semantics: HTTP transport only attempts to connect ONCE at session start if unreachable then — it never lazy-retries later even if the server comes up mid-session (a documented Claude Code limitation, GitHub issue #31198) — so the HTTP form structurally *requires* a server that is already alive before every session starts. stdio has no such requirement: Claude Code spawns the process itself at session start, reused for the rest of that session (confirmed: spawned once per session at init, not per tool call). The earlier '3 failures within one session' is more likely explained by a separate, documented dual-spawn bug (GitHub issue #85895: an unmanaged instance at t+0 plus a managed instance at t+2s within the same launch) than by genuine repeated reconnection attempts. Default switched BACK to stdio, fixed to call the globally-installed `playwright-mcp` binary directly (no `npx`), removing the dominant overhead that caused the original failures — see install.playwright below. RE-TESTED 2026-09-27, real: 1 solo run + 2 concurrent runs (with a semgrep scan running alongside as extra load) via fresh `claude -p` sessions calling `mcp__playwright__browser_navigate`/`browser_take_screenshot` — 3/3 clean, no timeouts. Residual accepted risk: under heavy concurrent system load at the exact moment a session starts, this spawn can still occasionally miss the connect timeout; this is a per-session-start risk, not a 'server is down' failure, and it cannot be fully eliminated without reintroducing a standing server. See adapters/playwright-mcp.md for the full sourced writeup.

agent-skills@addy-agent-skills: # CONFIRMED bug, fixed here: every entry in this install map used to be written with a leading slash (`/plugin marketplace add ...`, `/plugin install ...`) — that's Claude Code's INTERACTIVE slash-command syntax, meant to be typed by a human inside a live session; it is not a real shell command, and (per this skill's own specialist-runner.md A.2 findings about slash commands) an agent emitting that text doesn't trigger it either. Running it via Bash literally tries to execute a file at the path `/plugin` and fails with 'No such file or directory'. This silently worked for THIS specific entry only because the plugin had already been installed manually (with the correct syntax) before `check_or_install` ever exercised its install branch — the same latent bug went undetected here until superpowers (which had never been pre-installed) hit it for real in a genuine check_setup.sh --install run. The real, working form is the `claude` CLI's own subcommands (no leading slash), confirmed by actually running them: `claude plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>` and `claude plugin install <ref>`. Separately, on this machine `claude plugin install` for this specific plugin failed cloning via SSH (git@github.com:, no known host key / no SSH key on this account) even though the marketplace itself was already on disk — fixed by making git rewrite SSH github URLs to HTTPS globally: git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf "git@github.com:" (works anonymously for public repos, no key/credential needed). Re-check this if install fails fresh on another machine.
semgrep: # CONFIRMED this run, in 2 stages: (1) pip installs semgrep's binary into a Python "scripts" dir that isn't on PATH by default (Windows example seen: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Python\pythoncore-3.14-64\Scripts) — earlier versions of this entry only had a comment describing this, no command that actually fixed it, so the very next presence re-check still failed even though the install itself succeeded. (2) On git-bash/MSYS (Windows), that scripts dir comes back from Python's own sysconfig as a native Windows path (`C:\...`) — appending THAT raw string to bash's PATH does NOT work, `which`/`command -v` need POSIX form (`/c/...`); confirmed appending the raw Windows path left `which semgrep` still failing even though the string was genuinely in $PATH. The line below fixes both: sysconfig for the real location (portable to Mac/Linux too, where it's already POSIX and this is a no-op), `cygpath -u` to convert it when on git-bash/MSYS (falls back to the raw path if `cygpath` isn't present, e.g. native Linux/Mac). IMPORTANT — this export only survives within a single shell process: if your environment runs each install line as a SEPARATE process/tool call (this harness's own Bash tool documents that its shell state does NOT persist between calls), chain install+export+the real command together with `&&` in one call instead of relying on a prior export still being in PATH later, or resolve semgrep's full path once this way and keep invoking that full path instead of the bare `semgrep` command for the rest of this run.
pip install semgrep && S=$(python3 -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_path('scripts'))") && export PATH="$PATH:$(command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1 && cygpath -u "$S" || echo "$S")"
playwright: # DEFAULT is stdio again as of v2.3a (was a standalone HTTP server in v2.1-v2.3) — the user explicitly does not want to run a persistent standing background server. The original 3/3 stdio timeout was measured to be dominated by `npx @playwright/mcp@latest`'s own ~5s registry/resolution overhead PER SPAWN, not something inherent to stdio itself — fixed here by calling the already-installed global binary directly, skipping npx entirely. Per Claude Code's own MCP docs (checked 2026-09-27): a stdio server is spawned ONCE per session at init and reused for the rest of that session, not re-spawned per tool call — so this is a one-time per-session startup cost, not a per-call one. Every executable line below is idempotent — safe to re-run any time the specialist looks unusable. Residual accepted risk: under heavy concurrent system load at the exact moment a session starts, this spawn can still occasionally miss the connect timeout — there is no way to remove this risk entirely without a standing server (which the user rejected); see the HTTP alternative comment below if max reliability matters more than avoiding a background process.
claude mcp list 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^playwright:' || claude mcp add playwright -s user -- playwright-mcp --headless --isolated

# ALTERNATIVE (comment only, not auto-run) — trades 'no standing server' away for max reliability under heavy concurrent load: start `nohup playwright-mcp --port 8931 --headless --isolated > /tmp/playwright-mcp.log 2>&1 & disown` once as a long-lived background process, then `claude mcp add --transport http playwright http://localhost:8931/mcp -s user`. Confirmed 2/2 clean under real concurrent load in earlier testing (see specialists.frontend_live's note above) — but requires that process to survive across reboots/sessions, which is the exact overhead the current default was chosen to avoid. Only reconfigure to this form if the user asks for it.
